pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: crates/table-ledger/src/audit_detail.rs:512 The audit-action walk discards everything after a file's first #[cfg(test)], and that attribute also decorates single fields and statements, so production writers such as run.finish (engines.rs:481, after the marker at :474) and owner.decision (service.rs:693, after the marker at :175) are never read while the floors stay satisfied.

techniques.evidence: crates/table-ledger/src/audit_detail.rs:512 The comment on line 511 claims the cut removes a test module, but the needle matches any use of the attribute, so the walk's haystack fails toward green. The same cut is repeated at line 595.

crates/table-ledger/src/lib.rs:131 Older-ledger fixtures are the current schema with hand-listed DROPs (tests.rs:209 leaves generation_at in a 'v5' store), a shape no real older file has, and production carries the !has_reset_column branches (lib.rs:137, :146) only to tolerate it.
crates/table-ledger/src/audit_detail.rs:507 The walk declares floors on files and matches, which catch an empty walk but not the partial truncation recorded above.
crates/table-ledger/src/live_deals_tests.rs:255 The only elapsed-time measurement found in the listed files is an ignored probe that prints and asserts no duration.
crates/table-ledger/src/tests.rs:17 Each test gets a private in-memory store built by the real migration chain, so it cannot go stale; the per-test cost was not measured.
crates/table-ledger/src/lib.rs:74 The file-backed open that production uses and the in-memory fixture share one construction function.

pairs.registryProposal: pin-the-call-not-the-name could name the section-boundary case: a needle used to cut a file at its test section also matches the same attribute on single fields and statements, and a count floor cannot see that partial truncation because the remaining files still clear it.
